verses.text: Judah's descendants were Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Shobal's son Reaiah was the father of Jahath. Jahath was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.
These were the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah and the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah gave birth to Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were Naarah's sons.
Helah's sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
Hakkoz was the father of Anub and Zobebah, and the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was more respected than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez, saying, "I gave birth to him in pain."
Jabez prayed to the God of Israel, "Please bless me and give me more land! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm, so that I will not have pain!" And God gave him what he asked for.
Chelub, Shuhah's brother, was the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton was the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of Ir Nahash. These were the men of Recah.
Kenaz's sons were Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's son was Hathath.
Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who founded Ge Harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, because its people were skilled workers.
The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh were Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
Ezrah's sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. One of Mered's wives gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.

His wife from Judah gave birth to Jered, the father of Gedor, Heber, the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah. The others were the children of Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered had married.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's descendants were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah son of Judah were Er, the father of Lecah, Laadah, the father of Mareshah, and the clans of linen workers at Beth Ashbea.
There were also Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi Lehem. These records come from very ancient times.
They were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah. They lived there and worked for the king.
Simeon's sons were Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shaul's son was Shallum. Shallum's son was Mibsam. Mibsam's son was Mishma.
Mishma's descendants were his son Hammuel, Hammuel's son Zaccur, and Zaccur's son Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. But his brothers did not have many children, so their whole clan did not grow as large as the tribe of Judah.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David became king.
Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five towns,
along with all the villages around these towns as far as Baal. These were the places where they lived, and they kept a record of their family history.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah.
These men named here were leaders of their clans. Their families grew very large.
They went as far as the entrance to Gedor, to the east side of the valley, looking for pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture there. The land was wide open, quiet, and peaceful. Some descendants of Ham had lived there before.

These men whose names are listed came during the time of Hezekiah king of Judah. They attacked the Hamites in their tents and the Meunites who lived there, and destroyed them completely, as can still be seen today. Then they settled in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
Five hundred of these Simeonites went to the hill country of Seir. Their leaders were Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They killed the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.
